limits: Process termination and returned I/O errors do not emulate physical power loss.
Interruption points start after ownership records are durably established.
Traditional inode/single-block xattrs; EA_INODE and RichACL inheritance are not supported.
Linux inode layout and existing dirty/recovery/feature guards apply.
Kernel verification uses Linux in WSL2; editing uses native Windows backend/worker.

MSVC backends differ in PE/debug timestamps and the case of embedded Cargo registry diagnostic paths. The report preserves actual hashes and proves all other bytes identical; those source directory aliases resolve to the same filesystem object.
No macOS/ARM64, physical power loss, full capacity/depth limit or physical-partition write claim is made.
